scenarios.name: count-ten-million-accounts
scenarios.why: #7954: SELECT COUNT(*) over 10,000,001 ACCOUNT rows of sort code 987654 gives NUMBER-OF-ACCOUNTS 10000001, whose first digit shows when the typed record reads ACCOUNT-CONTROL-NUMBER 9 wide or one byte late

scenarios.name: dto-entry-count-ten-million-accounts
scenarios.why: as count-ten-million-accounts, through the typed DTO alone: fill_ gives back the count 10000001, whose first digit shows when fill_ reads ACCOUNT-CONTROL-NUMBER 9 wide or one byte late (#7954)

notes: Sibling of cbsa-acctctrl (#7954): the same ACCTCTRL program on a seed of 10,000,001 ACCOUNT rows for sort code 987654 (one recursive INSERT), so NUMBER-OF-ACCOUNTS reaches 8 digits with a leading 1. The main case's seed cannot reach it (reseeding per scenario is too costly). The table is not compared (10M rows); the program only reads it. Judged on the det port; synthetic data.
